summary: Private install: Grafana loads but no Redwood dashboards (minimum observability pack)
environment: prod | on-prem (air-gapped) | k8s v1.28 | RHEL9 nodes
description:
Issue summary
- Customer completed Redwood Private install (including the “observability minimum pack”). Grafana UI is reachable and Prometheus is scraping targets, but there are no Redwood dashboards visible under Browse/Dashboards.

Customer impact
- Customer platform team cannot validate runtime health post-install and is blocked on their internal acceptance checklist for go-live.
- No production outage, but reduces operational visibility and delays launch.

Customer environment (as provided)
- Deployment type: On-prem / air-gapped
- Installer version: redwood-private-installer v1.12.3 (offline bundle)
- Helm charts: redwood-helm-charts 1.12.3
- Observability pack: included in offline bundle (customer unsure which pack version)
- Namespace(s): redwood-system (control plane), redwood-runtime (data plane), monitoring (Grafana/Prometheus)
- Grafana: 10.4.x (from our bundled chart)
- Prometheus: kube-prometheus-stack (bundled)
- StorageClass: longhorn
- NetworkPolicies: enabled (customer baseline)

What’s expected
- Redwood-provisioned dashboards should appear automatically (Runtime Overview, Control Plane Health, GPU Fleet, etc.) in Grafana under a “Redwood” folder (or similarly named folder) after install.

What’s observed
- Grafana is up and login works.
- Datasource exists (“Prometheus”) and can query basic metrics (up, kube_pod_info).
- No dashboards in the Redwood folder; in some cases no Redwood folder at all.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Install Redwood Private with observability pack enabled using offline bundle.
2) Access Grafana -> Dashboards.
3) Observe no Redwood dashboards.

Initial hypotheses
- Dashboards ConfigMaps not present in cluster (missing from offline bundle or Helm values disabled).
- ConfigMaps present but not labeled for Grafana sidecar discovery.
- Grafana sidecar for dashboards disabled or misconfigured (watch namespace/label selector mismatch).
- Grafana provisioning path not mounted / permissions issue.
- RBAC preventing Grafana sidecar from listing ConfigMaps in target namespaces.

Key customer-provided snippets
1) kubectl get cm -n monitoring | grep -i redwood => (empty)
2) kubectl get pods -n monitoring => grafana-xxxxx Running
3) Grafana logs (excerpt):
   - "logger=provisioning.dashboard t=2025-07-18T16:02:11.913Z level=info msg=\"Starting Dashboard provisioning\""
   - No subsequent "Dashboard provisioned" entries

Support request
- Identify whether dashboards were packaged/applied.
- Provide a workaround to get dashboards installed in Grafana for air-gapped cluster.
- Confirm the correct Helm values/settings for the minimum pack and whether any known issue exists in v1.12.3 offline bundle.

Resolution summary (final)
- Root cause: Grafana dashboards were included in the cluster as ConfigMaps, but Grafana’s dashboard sidecar was watching only the monitoring namespace and a different label key than what the Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps used in 1.12.3 offline bundle. Additionally, RBAC was missing list/watch on ConfigMaps in redwood-system/redwood-runtime.
- Fix: Update Helm values to (a) align the sidecar label selector with the Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps and (b) allow cross-namespace discovery OR copy dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring. Applied RBAC fix and restarted Grafana.
- Outcome: Redwood dashboards appeared under folder “Redwood Private (Minimum Pack)” within 5 minutes; customer confirmed panels populated.

Workaround / customer steps (executed)
A) Confirm dashboards ConfigMaps exist:
- kubectl get cm -A | grep -E "redwood|observability|grafana-dashboard"

B) Update Grafana sidecar + RBAC (preferred) via values override:
- Set:
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.enabled=true
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.searchNamespace=ALL
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.label=grafana_dashboard
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.labelValue="1"
- Add RBAC for grafana sidecar service account to list/watch ConfigMaps in redwood-system and redwood-runtime.
- Helm upgrade kube-prometheus-stack / grafana release.

C) Restart Grafana:
- kubectl rollout restart deploy/grafana -n monitoring

D) Validate:
- Grafana -> Dashboards -> folder appears
- Prometheus datasource queries for redwood_* recording rules and runtime metrics return data

Notes
- If customer security policy blocks searchNamespace=ALL, alternative is copying the dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace with the expected label (documented below in comments).
comments:
2025-07-18 09:12 (Dev Patel - Support)
Created ticket from customer email + #support handoff. Requested environment details and installer/Helm versions. Asked for: `kubectl get cm -A | grep grafana` and Grafana pod logs around provisioning start.

2025-07-18 10:03 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
Install finished successfully and health checks passed. We can log into Grafana, Prometheus datasource works, but there are no Redwood dashboards. `kubectl get cm -n monitoring | grep -i redwood` returns nothing. We are air-gapped and used the offline bundle from Redwood. NetworkPolicies are enabled cluster-wide.

2025-07-18 10:26 (Bruno Silva - PS / Private Deployments)
Likely either (1) dashboards not applied because the pack values were off, or (2) dashboards are created in a different namespace than Grafana’s sidecar is watching. Can you run `kubectl get cm -A | grep -i grafana` and `kubectl describe deploy grafana -n monitoring` (look for sidecar args)?

2025-07-18 11:02 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
`kubectl get cm -A | grep -i grafana` shows:
- redwood-system/redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1
- redwood-runtime/redwood-runtime-dashboards-1
Both have labels:
- app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm
- redwood.ai/observability-pack=true
No label like grafana_dashboard=1.
`kubectl describe deploy grafana -n monitoring` shows sidecar enabled but label selector is `grafana_dashboard=1` and namespace is monitoring only.

2025-07-18 11:20 (Dylan Brooks - Dashboards/tooling)
That explains it: our dashboard ConfigMaps in 1.12.3 are labeled `redwood.ai/observability-pack=true` (not `grafana_dashboard=1`). Either update sidecar label selector to match our label, or (safer) add `grafana_dashboard=1` label to the existing ConfigMaps. Also, sidecar is only monitoring namespace; if ConfigMaps live in redwood-system/redwood-runtime you need searchNamespace=ALL or copy the ConfigMaps into monitoring.
Proposed immediate workaround:
1) Label ConfigMaps: `kubectl label cm -n redwood-system redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1 grafana_dashboard=1 --overwrite` and same for runtime.
2) Set sidecar searchNamespace=ALL (or copy CMs to monitoring if ALL is disallowed).
3) Restart Grafana deployment.
Longer-term we should align the Helm chart defaults/labels for private minimum pack.

2025-07-18 12:05 (Bruno Silva - PS / Private Deployments)
Customer prefers not to run sidecar across all namespaces due to security review. Suggested option: copy dashboards ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace.
Commands:
- `kubectl get cm -n redwood-system redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1 -o yaml | sed 's/namespace: redwood-system/namespace: monitoring/' | kubectl apply -n monitoring -f -`
- Repeat for `redwood-runtime/redwood-runtime-dashboards-1`
- Label the new CMs: `kubectl label cm -n monitoring <cm-name> grafana_dashboard=1 --overwrite`
Then restart Grafana.
Also asked customer to confirm Grafana SA has list/watch on ConfigMaps in monitoring (it does by default).

2025-07-18 14:18 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
We copied both ConfigMaps into monitoring and labeled `grafana_dashboard=1`. After restarting Grafana, we now see a “Redwood Private (Minimum Pack)” folder and dashboards are present. Panels were initially empty; after ~2 minutes they started populating. This unblocks us.
Question: is there an official supported fix so we don’t have to maintain copies after upgrades?

2025-07-18 15:01 (Dev Patel - Support)
Confirmed the workaround is acceptable short-term but we want a supported path. Looping in SRE/Telemetry to confirm recommended values for private minimum pack. Also linking runbook: private observability day-2 operations (Grafana provisioning section).

2025-07-19 09:42 (Rafael Mendes - SRE)
Recommendation for supported installs: either (A) keep dashboards in monitoring namespace to avoid cross-namespace watch, or (B) explicitly enable cross-namespace watch and add RBAC for grafana sidecar. For Private minimum pack we should default to (A) in air-gapped bundles to reduce security friction.
Also noted we’ve had a similar CI failure in INT-11804 where dashboards weren’t discovered due to label mismatch.

2025-07-19 11:10 (Connor O'Brien - Release/packaging)
Checked offline bundle manifest for 1.12.3: dashboards are included, but labels differ from kube-prometheus-stack defaults. This is tracked for backport in the private installer/helm wiring. Suggest we point customer to upgrading to 1.12.4 once released (will include corrected labels and/or chart values).

2025-07-21 16:30 (Dev Patel - Support)
Customer confirmed stable after 48h. No further action needed on their side until next upgrade. We provided guidance for keeping the copy step as part of their upgrade runbook if they remain on 1.12.3.
Closing ticket as resolved with workaround + upcoming product fix.
Internal follow-up: ensure minimum pack dashboards ship with `grafana_dashboard=1` (or chart default label is updated) and install places dashboards in monitoring namespace for air-gapped installs.
resolution: Resolved via workaround: copied Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace and labeled for Grafana sidecar discovery; restarted Grafana. Customer validated dashboards present and populated. Product follow-up identified to align labels/defaults in subsequent Private releases.
customer_visible_next_steps: If you upgrade Redwood Private before the label/namespace fix is included, re-run the dashboard copy + label step (or opt into cross-namespace sidecar watch with RBAC). We will notify you once the supported default is available in a maintenance release.
internal_follow_ups: Validate and backport dashboard label alignment for Private offline bundles (air-gapped) so kube-prometheus-stack Grafana sidecar discovers Redwood dashboards without manual copy.
Update Private day-2 runbook to include detection steps: where dashboards ConfigMaps live, required labels, and namespace watch settings.
